entities.name: Gurguit Barbtruc
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Gurguit Barbtruc was a legendary king of the Britons as accounted by Geoffrey of Monmouth. He was the son of Belinus and was said to have found a home for the Irish people.

Gurguit Barbtruc's reign is believed to have taken place in the 5th or 6th century AD, during a time of significant cultural and linguistic change in Britain. His story has been passed down through the centuries, influencing later historical accounts and literary works.

The legacy of Gurguit Barbtruc extends beyond his own time and place, reflecting the complex and often fraught relationships between ancient Celtic cultures. His story serves as a reminder of the enduring power of myth and legend to shape our understanding of the past.

In the words of Geoffrey of Monmouth, 'Gurguit, son of Belinus, was the first king of the Britons, who, in his time, was most noble and most wise, and who, with the help of his gods, was most successful in his conquests.'
